question_en:
I am organizing investor relations materials for an industrial company and wish to compare the safety image on the annual report covers with changes in R&D investment. The attachment shows a work scene used on one of the annual report covers. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which company and which Annual Report year does the material in the image come from?
2. Taking all Annual Reports published by the company from 2017 to 2024 as the scope, examine each cover one by one. In which years does the cover show at least one person wearing both a hard hat and clearly visible goggles or safety glasses? According to the official annual reports, what were the sales and revenues, R&D expense, and R&D intensity for those identified years?

Response format: Please answer in numbered points (1)–(2); answer question 1 in text; for question 2, use a table to list all identified years year by year along with their sales and revenues, R&D expense, and R&D intensity, specifying the units; do not list the years separately.
answer:
(1) Company: Caterpillar Inc.; Annual Report year: 2019.

(2)

| Identified Year | sales and revenues (million USD) | R&D expense (million USD) | R&D intensity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2017 | 45,462 | 1,842 | 4.1% |
| 2019 | 53,800 | 1,693 | 3.1% |

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-8-3-G01

## Step 01 · Identify cover source from CAT and work scene

Action: Observe yellow CAT hard hat, reflective vest, two personnel, safety glasses on the right, and quarry background; example query: Caterpillar annual report cover two workers quarry CAT 2019.

Evidence observation: The current attachment shows a work scene, not the full report cover. The CAT logo provides a company candidate; the report year must be verified against the official PDF cover and cannot be guessed from equipment age or image upload path.

Evidence links:
https://www.caterpillar.com/en/investors/reports/reports-archive.html

Result of this step: Enter Caterpillar investor relations archive.

## Step 02 · Match attachment to 2019 Annual Report

Action: Open the first page of the 2019 Annual Report in the official archive and compare the posture of the two workers, the yellow hard hats, and the quarry background.

Evidence observation: The same work scene corresponds to Caterpillar Inc.'s 2019 Annual Report. The URL resource name contains CM20210503, but this is part of the file resource path and does not equal the report year 2021.

Evidence links:
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210503-db4c9-8a1a2

Result of this step: Company and report year for Question 1 are determined.

## Step 03 · Lock the complete set of eight Annual Reports

Action: Enumerate Annual Reports in the official report archive by the question's year range 2017–2024, avoiding mixing in Proxy Statements or Quarterly Reports.

Evidence observation: The closed set has 8 years; for each year, take the first page of the Annual Report PDF as the cover. Upload month/year in PDF filenames, webpage update dates, and financial report years are recorded separately; historical reports are not discarded due to later uploads.

## Step 04 · Define dual-protection condition for the same person

Action: Examine the head and eye area of persons on each cover one by one to determine whether the same person is wearing both a hard hat and clearly visible goggles or safety glasses.

Evidence observation: One person wearing a hat and another wearing glasses does not satisfy the "simultaneous" condition; ordinary hats, masks, and reflective vests do not substitute for hard hats; blurry cab areas cannot have protective equipment inferred based on common occupational knowledge.

Result of this step: First filter years by visual conditions, then read financial values for identified years.

## Step 05 · Check 2017 Annual Report cover by cover

Action: View the first page of that year's PDF, lock onto the cover rather than the table of contents, inner pages, or webpage promotional images; check the head and eye area of each visible person one by one.

Evidence observation: The worker at the bottom left of the cover is wearing both a hard hat and clear eye protection; at least one person satisfies both conditions.

## Step 12 · Check 2024 Annual Report cover by cover

Action: View the first page of that year's PDF, lock onto the cover rather than the table of contents, inner pages, or webpage promotional images; check the head and eye area of each visible person one by one.

Evidence observation: The cab area is insufficient to clearly confirm both items of equipment on the same person; does not reach the clarity threshold and cannot be counted by speculation.

Evidence links:
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20250506-c118a-5d3cb

Result of this step: 2024: Excluded; do not enter the final financial results table.

## Step 13 · Verify eight-year coverage and identified set

Action: Sort visual results by year and check whether each year from 2017 to 2024 has exactly one entry.

Evidence observation: Identified 2017 and 2019; excluded 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024; 2 + 6 = 8; did not skip any PDF because a certain year had no obvious persons. Next, extract financial indicators only for the two identified years.

Evidence links:
https://www.caterpillar.com/en/investors/reports/reports-archive.html

Result of this step: Avoid first learning the financial years and then working backward to look at only two covers.

## Step 14 · Locate financial summary page with consistent scope

Action: In the 2019 Annual Report's Five-year Financial Summary, check Sales and revenues, Research and development expenses, and their percentage.

Evidence observation: Physical PDF page 29 corresponds to Form 10-K printed page 17; table headers span multiple years, and the 2017 column and 2019 column must be aligned separately. Amount units are millions of dollars, not dollars or billions of dollars; percentages are as a percent of sales and revenues as listed in the annual report.

Evidence links:
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210503-db4c9-8a1a2

Result of this step: Use the same summary table to cross-cover the two identified years.

## Step 15 · Extract 2017 data and verify percentage

Action: In the 2017 column, record sales and revenues, R&D expenses, and the disclosed R&D percentage, then use division to check the order of magnitude.

Evidence observation: Sales and revenues = 45,462 million USD; R&D = 1,842 million USD; annual report discloses 4.1%. 1,842 ÷ 45,462 × 100 is approximately 4.05%, consistent with the disclosed 4.1% rounded to one decimal place. Do not mismatch values from adjacent years in the amount columns.

Evidence links:
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20190503-bda43-dfbbd
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210503-db4c9-8a1a2

Result of this step: The three indicators for the 2017 row are complete.

## Step 16 · Extract 2019 data and verify scope

Action: Read the three indicators from the 2019 column in the same summary table, using the same units and display precision.

Evidence observation: Sales and revenues=53800 million USD; R&D=1693 million USD; disclosed as 3.1%. 1693÷53800×100 is approximately 3.147%, which rounds to 3.1% when kept to one decimal place; the officially disclosed value must not be altered to pursue more decimal places.

Evidence link:
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210503-db4c9-8a1a2

Result of this step: The 2019 row is complete with all three indicators.

## Step 17 · Exclude extended calculations not asked in the question

Action: Verify that the question requires only the identified years and the three indicators; do not add R&D amounts for all eight years or infer a causal relationship between safety imagery and investment.

Evidence observation: The difference between 4.1% and 3.1% is 1.0 percentage points, which can be used for internal consistency checks, but since the question does not ask for the difference, this column is not added to the final table. Cover visual screening and financial verification are two types of evidence; the former does not explain the reasons for changes in R&D.

Evidence link:
https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210503-db4c9-8a1a2

Result of this step: The answer maintains two rows and clear units; the process retains sources from eight PDFs.

## Step 18 · Verify question requirements and output scope

Action: Correspond each mandatory public item with the evidence above, checking the total count, positive/negative items, and field formats.

Evidence observation: The company, 2019 cover identity, the full set of eight years, year-by-year visual exclusions, and the 2017/2019 financial fields all correspond; the final list includes only the two identified years.

Result of this step: Write only the requested information into the final answer; keep the search process and exclusion basis in the trajectory.
